memory_annotations.evidence_summary: Kara chose the GSP routing, compact pay-later rental, and mountain lodge after comparing recovery amenities against downtown convenience. She wanted booking caveats stated before purchase, prioritized adjacent seats with her partner, selected the window seat for herself, and added a late-arrival and food-plan note.

verified_habit_signals.evidence_quote: Put me at the window and him next to me.

messages.content: My partner says the lodge drive is okay as long as we're not committing to a sketchy road after dark. Can you do the final practical check and then book the GSP version if the caveats look clean?

I rechecked the three paths. Practical pick is still GSP + compact rental + mountain lodge. It is about 55-65 minutes after landing, but it is highway and paved state roads if you ignore the gravel shortcut some map apps suggest. It prices better than flying into Asheville by about $170 per person, and the rental is pay-later. The lodge is pricier than downtown, but it keeps the pool, hot tub, and fitness room plus the queen room with coffee maker and mini-fridge. Downtown Asheville wins on dinner convenience, but it has no hot tub and only a small fitness room. If this weekend is hiking recovery first, I would book the lodge.
Okay. Book GSP and the lodge. I want refundable where it actually matters, not a bargain that traps us.

Before I press purchase: flights are Main Cabin, not Basic, because Basic would not let us select adjacent seats now. The lodge takes a one-night deposit but cancels free until June 19 at 4 p.m.; after that the first night is the penalty. Compact car is pay at pickup and can be canceled before pickup. That is the cleanest set of caveats I found.
Use Main Cabin. For seats, together matters more than squeezing out a few dollars. What are the choices?

On the Tampa-GSP routing through Atlanta, the no-extra pairs are A/B in row 18 on both legs Thursday, and A/B in rows 17 and 20 on the Monday return. That means one window and one middle. Across-the-aisle aisle seats are available on one segment, but not all four segments without an upgrade.
A/B is fine. Put me at the window and him next to me.

Got it. I have you in 18A and him in 18B for the Thursday flights; return is 17A/17B on GSP-ATL and 20A/20B on ATL-TPA. Flight timing: Thursday leaves TPA 5:18 p.m., lands GSP 8:38 p.m.; Monday leaves GSP 1:55 p.m. and gets you back to Tampa 5:27 p.m.
Check late arrival at the lodge before you book it. I don't want a locked front desk if Atlanta goes sideways.

I called the lodge. Front desk is staffed until 11 p.m.; after that they use a lockbox and text the code if your flight is delayed. I added your flight number to the reservation note and a request not to route you up the gravel back road. Hot tub and pool are open until 10, so Thursday is probably just check-in and sleep.
That's fine. Book the car pay-later too. Compact is enough unless the price jump to midsize is tiny.
Compact is $238 all-in, pay at pickup. Midsize is $291, so I kept compact. Counter hours cover the scheduled arrival, and the rental reservation has the flight number attached. No prepaid penalty.
Great. Add a food note. We're not going to hunt for dinner at 10 p.m.

Booked and noted. Confirmations are: Delta itinerary K8F2QH, lodge reservation ML-63048, rental GSP-8421KB. Arrival plan is snack or quick pickup before leaving the airport/Greer, then straight to the lodge by the main-road route. Caveats to keep visible: lodge free-cancel deadline June 19 at 4 p.m., one-night deposit now, compact rental pay-later, and Thursday hot tub access is unlikely because of arrival time.

memory_annotations.evidence_summary: Kara kept the lodge despite the first-night hot tub closure because the closure should end before the main hiking days and switching was costly. She accepted a king room as a possible resort fallback, but only if the hot tub delay extended past Friday. Trail plans were adjusted around the closure.

verified_habit_signals.evidence_quote: Keep the lodge unless they push the hot tub past Friday.
King room at the resort doesn't bother me.

messages.content: The lodge just emailed that the hot tub is closed the first night for resurfacing. Also the trail we liked is closed. Is this a keep-it or switch situation?

I checked the alternatives. The lodge closure is Thursday only, with pool and fitness room open and hot tub reopening Friday afternoon. Since you land late Thursday, you probably would not use it that night anyway. The resort nearby has an outdoor hot tub open and a 4.6 rating, but only king rooms left and it is about $410 more for the stay. The cabin has a kitchenette and more quiet, but no fitness access and no hotel-style recovery setup.
So the resort is the only real upgrade, but expensive. What's the cancellation clock on the lodge?

Lodge can still cancel without penalty until Friday at 4 p.m. The resort becomes nonrefundable after 24 hours from booking, and the cabin keeps 50% once booked. If you switch, the resort is the safer experience but the least flexible.
King room at the resort doesn't bother me. The extra $410 does. What about the trail closure?

The ridge loop you marked first is closed for maintenance through the weekend. Best replacement: do a shorter Friday hike at Bearwallow or Pink Beds after the travel day, then make Saturday the longer Looking Glass Rock option if weather is stable. That keeps the lodge location useful.
Keep the lodge unless they push the hot tub past Friday. Can you verify that reopening isn't just wishful thinking?

Front desk says resurfacing is scheduled Thursday morning, cure time Thursday night, chemical balancing Friday late morning, and guest access expected by 2 p.m. Friday. They said they will email if weather delays it.
Okay. Add a reminder before the cancellation deadline, and switch Friday to the shorter hike.

Done. We are keeping the lodge for now, with a Friday noon reminder before the 4 p.m. free-cancel deadline. If the hot tub slips beyond Friday, the resort becomes the only worthwhile switch; otherwise the lodge still fits the weekend better. Trail plan is now shorter Friday, longer Saturday, with no change to flights or rental.

memory_annotations.evidence_summary: For Columbus, Kara prioritized a reliable room setup over the shortest commute, accepted a better-rated suite hotel without a hot tub, added a rental car to avoid early rideshare uncertainty, preferred a Sunday afternoon return over risky Saturday options, and selected window seats while delaying booking until hospital logistics are confirmed.

verified_habit_signals.evidence_quote: Can the suite confirm actual queen, coffee, and fridge? Not a request basis?
Can the suite confirm actual queen, coffee, and fridge? Not a request basis?
No hot tub is disappointing but acceptable here.

messages.content: New one: Columbus Children's wants me for the pediatric neuro-motor lab Friday-Saturday, Aug 21-22. They want a Thursday evening room walk-through, and Saturday teardown could be done at 3:30 or drift to 5. I can leave Tampa after my noon faculty call. Can you build the practical flight/hotel version, not just cheapest?
Yes. Two things before I narrow it: is the Thursday walk-through truly required before Friday morning, and are you willing to stay Saturday night if that keeps the return from being a scramble?
Walk-through is pretty important because I need to see mat spacing and where the treatment tables land. I'm willing to stay Saturday night. I don't want a midnight return after teaching.

Then I would not anchor this around the cheapest connection. Flight shortlist: 1) late-afternoon nonstop TPA-CMH Thursday, arrives about 6:45 p.m.; workable for a 7:30-ish walk-through. 2) lower-fare connection through ATL/CLT, arrives around 10:55 p.m.; cheaper but it misses the useful walk-through window and makes Friday rough. For return, Saturday 6:40 p.m. only works if teardown really ends at 3:30; Sunday early afternoon is the calmer plan.
Agreed. Hotel is where I need the real comparison. There's something right by the hospital, but the reviews looked uneven.

I see the same split. Hospital-adjacent hotel: fastest commute, possibly walkable or a very short drive, about $186/night, overall rating around 4.0 but recent reviews mention AC noise, slow housekeeping, and mini-fridges not guaranteed in every room. Fitness room is small; no hot tub. Suite hotel 15 minutes away: about $164/night, 4.4 rating, queen studio confirmed with coffee maker and mini-fridge, indoor pool and fitness room, no hot tub. Airport hotel is cheaper, but it puts you farther from the lab and does not help Thursday walkthrough.
The suite sounds more reliable. The only issue is the 15-minute drive before an early lab. I don't want to be waiting on rideshare at 6:45.

Then pair the suite with a small rental car. Compact rental is about $112 total from Thursday evening to Sunday midday, cancellable, and the suite has free parking. That makes the morning predictable. The hospital-adjacent option saves drive time, but it adds room uncertainty right before two teaching days.
Can the suite confirm actual queen, coffee, and fridge? Not a request basis?

Yes. I called reservations: queen studio is a bookable room type, not just a preference. In-room coffee maker and mini-fridge are standard in that room; microwave too. Indoor pool and fitness room are open 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. The missing recovery item is the hot tub; they do not have one.
No hot tub is disappointing but acceptable here. Reliability beats being across the street. What do we need from the hospital before I let you book?

I would ask them for five confirmations: Thursday room access by 7:30 p.m.; exact loading/parking entrance and whether the rental can be left there during setup; secure overnight storage for mats/demo gear Friday night; whether teardown is expected at 3:30 or they need you held until 5; and a named on-site contact for AV, table count, and room unlocks.
Add whether I can leave gear there Saturday while I return the rental or if it has to be out immediately.
Added. That matters for the return choice too. If gear has to be out immediately and teardown slides, a Saturday flight gets much uglier.
Show me the Saturday versus Sunday return in plain terms.

Saturday 6:40 p.m. nonstop: fine only if teardown ends 3:30, gear is packed by 4:15, and you leave the hospital by 4:30. Any slip makes it stressful. Saturday 8:55 p.m. connection: technically possible after a 5 p.m. finish, but it gets you to Tampa after midnight. Sunday 1:42 p.m. nonstop: lets you finish the course, sleep, return the car without rushing, and land in Tampa around 3:55 p.m. The Sunday fare is about $46 more than the late Saturday connection.
Sunday 1:42 is the one. If the hospital complains about another hotel night, I want the reason spelled out.

Reason: their schedule has an unresolved 3:30-to-5:00 teardown window, and the late finish makes same-day return either risky or a post-midnight connection. Staying Saturday protects course wrap-up, gear handling, and your ability to function Monday.
For fares, don't use basic if seats are random. I need to pick now.

Main Cabin is the right fare here. It is $38 more than Basic on the outbound and $34 more on the return, but it includes seat selection and avoids check-in-only assignment. Current seat map has 12A on the Thursday nonstop and 14A on the Sunday return, plus several aisle seats if you prefer those.
Window is good. Hold 12A and 14A. Do not ticket until the hospital answers the access/storage questions.

Held, not ticketed. Working Columbus plan is: Thu Aug 20 late-afternoon nonstop TPA-CMH in Main Cabin, seat 12A; compact rental at CMH, cancellable; queen studio at the better-rated suite hotel Aug 20-23 with coffee maker, mini-fridge, indoor pool, and fitness room but no hot tub; Sun Aug 23 1:42 p.m. nonstop back to Tampa, seat 14A. I drafted the hospital email with the access, loading, secure storage, gear-removal, and Saturday finish-time questions. Once they confirm, this is the practical version to book.
